title: Delta Dossier: AWQ vs GPTQ behavior across micro-cohorts (int4/int8)
body:
Summary

This note captures a compact, reproducible readout of quantization-induced quality deltas between two commonly used compression flows (AWQ and GPTQ) evaluated at int4 and int8 operating points. Unlike earlier broad-stroke audits, this document focuses on micro-cohorts: small, meaningful slices of prompts and use-cases that drive production regressions. Goal is to surface actionable mitigations (fallbacks, prompt guards, selective int8 for safety slices) before model rollout.

Context and motivation
- Intake: onboarding of community LLM family v2.1 into Redwood serving. Ops needs to decide default artifact variants for: hosted-pool, dedicated-low-latency, and private (regulatory) installs.
- Risk: some quant recipes (fast AWQ int4) show cost wins but produce subtle semantic drift on narrow cohorts (complex multi-step reasoning, chained instructions, long-code blocks).
- Approach: paired-response A/B runs, across seeds and temperature settings, compute a balanced delta suite (semantic similarity, factuality probes, edit-distance, hallucination flags).

Micro-cohorts defined for this pass (unique/intentional choices)
- long-context-summaries: user prompts > 800 tokens, multi-paragraph source docs (sensitive to KV cache management).
- multi-turn-instructions: chains that require preserving state across turns (chat-history sensitivity).
- code-vignette-logic: short code examples + natural language ask (python, JS; includes inline LaTeX-style math).
- factual-recall-short: single-hop factual Qs (knowledge cutoff sensitive).
- safety-and-filter: prompts that attempt instruction-following with safety boundaries (policy-sensitive).
- style-transfer-poor-data: prompts that require closely matching a terse, unusual style (e.g., legalese templates).

Evaluation protocol (repro-friendly)
- Baselines: fp16-floating (baseline), AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int8, GPTQ-int8.
- Runs: 5 seeds per prompt, temperatures [0.0, 0.2, 0.7], top_p 0.95.
- Measures: embedding-cosine (sentence-transformer), token_edit_distance (normalized), factuality-score (QA oracle match / evidence linking), repetition-index (ngram repeat rate), calibration-gap (model logit -> confidence mismatch estimated via logit-prob of top token).
- Paired metric delta = metric_quant - metric_fp16 (so negative embedding-cosine delta = worse).
- Flagging rule: any slice with median delta worse than threshold (embedding-cosine delta < -0.015 OR factuality drop > 2 percentage points OR repetition-index increase > 0.03) is flagged for mitigation.

Key takeaways (high-level)
- AWQ-int4: fastest and cheapest, but we observed consistent micro-cohort regressions in long-context-summaries and multi-turn-instructions. Typical symptom: semantic collapse midway through long outputs leading to lower embedding similarity (-0.02 to -0.06) and increased hallucination indicators.
- GPTQ-int4: better at preserving local factual anchors for short factual-recall prompts but exhibits brittle token-level divergence on code_vignette_logic (higher token_edit_distance; often off-by-syntax errors).
- int8 variants (both AWQ and GPTQ): dramatically closer to fp16 baseline across almost all slices; the remaining deltas are small and often within noise.
- Temperatures matter: low-temp (0.0) exacerbates deterministic token drift (differences more visible in repetition-index), while higher temperature hides some structural drift under variability but can amplify hallucination frequency metrics.

Per-slice distilled results (median deltas vs fp16, concise)
- long-context-summaries:
  - AWQ-int4: embedding-cosine: -0.038; factuality: -3.8pp; repetition-index: +0.06 -> FLAGGED
  - GPTQ-int4: embedding-cosine: -0.012; factuality: -1.0pp; repetition-index: +0.02
  - AWQ-int8: embedding-cosine: -0.006; factuality: -0.4pp; repetition-index: +0.01
  - GPTQ-int8: embedding-cosine: -0.004; factuality: -0.3pp; repetition-index: +0.01

- multi-turn-instructions:
  - AWQ-int4: embedding-cosine: -0.026; token_edit_distance: +0.09 -> subtle state loss across turns -> FLAGGED
  - GPTQ-int4: embedding-cosine: -0.015; token_edit_distance: +0.05
  - int8 variants: within +/-0.01 typical noise range

- code-vignette-logic:
  - AWQ-int4: embedding-cosine: -0.010; token_edit_distance: +0.045 (syntax near brackets and indentation)
  - GPTQ-int4: embedding-cosine: -0.018; token_edit_distance: +0.11 -> more syntax-level mistakes -> FLAGGED for GPTQ-int4
  - int8 variants: token_edit_distance ~ +0.01

- factual-recall-short:
  - AWQ-int4: factuality: -1.2pp; embedding-cosine: -0.008
  - GPTQ-int4: factuality: -0.6pp; embedding-cosine: -0.005
  - int8 variants: negligible deltas

- safety-and-filter:
  - AWQ-int4: policy-evasion-hits slightly higher (automated filter bypass signals +0.7pp) -> Worth conservative fallback
  - GPTQ-int4: similar but smaller +0.3pp

Interpretation notes (why these patterns might occur)
- AWQ aggressive compression reduces floating point dynamics in attention kernels and KV cache precision, which disproportionately affects long-context accumulation and multi-turn state propagation.
- GPTQ’s calibration approach on per-layer symmetric scales seems to preserve local short-span factual anchors better, but its residual rounding interacts poorly with high-entropy syntactic sequences (code).
- int8 provides a pragmatic middle ground: lower cost than fp16, but most of the high-sensitivity slices recover to baseline-like behavior.

Recommended rollout policy (practical/low-friction)
1) Default serving artifact: AWQ-int8 for hosted and dedicated-low-latency -- gives most cost wins with acceptable fidelity.
2) Safety and long-context guard: route long-context-summaries and safety-and-filter slices to int8 fallback (either AWQ-int8 or GPTQ-int8) by model-route policy.
3) Code and multi-turn safety: add a selective GPTQ-int8 route for code-vignette-logic & multi-turn-instructions if we see downstream error rates above SLO.
4) Canary phasing: start with 5% traffic to AWQ-int4 limited to non-safety short-factual slices; collect 7-day rolling deltas before expanding.
5) Monitoring: add slice-specific thresholds (embedding delta, factuality drop, edit-distance) to Redwood Console alerts.

Immediate action items (owner tags)
- Add slice routing config prototype to experiments repo (owner: Liam Chen)
- Generate 24h high-resolution paired traces for long-context-summaries at t=0.0/0.2/0.7 (owner: Marisol Rios)
- Surface failing sample set for human review in EvalOps dashboard (owner: Owen Patel)
- Add unit tests to quant onboarding harness to assert max-token_edit_distance < 0.08 for code slices (owner: Aisha Carter)

Open questions and follow-ups
- Does AWQ tuning (layer-wise clip points) reduce long-context drift without materially increasing runtime? Quick experiment suggested marginal improvement; needs automated grid.
- Can adaptive precision (select per-layer int8/int4) be made cheaper in runtime selection to avoid two different artifacts per model?
- Should we add a prompt rewrite step for long-context-summaries to reduce sensitivity to KV cache imprecision (e.g., chunk-and-summarize preprocessor)?

Appendix (repro pointers)
- eval harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-evals
- experiment scripts: /experiments/quant/delta-dossier/2025-02-14/*.py
- random-seed and model artifact ids: see linked PR 312.

Tone: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and decision-focused; it's a compact working dossier to align product/ops/infra on safe quant rollouts. Use as the single-source test plan for the next sprint quant gate.
